newsitem.title: USA: Utilicorp, PECO launch energy marketing company.
newsitem.headline: Utilicorp, PECO launch energy marketing company.

text.p: Faced with deregulation in their markets, Utilicorp United Inc. and Peco Energy Co. said Tuesday they would offer consumers one-stop shopping for natural gas, electricity, telephone and home security services.

The two companies said they will launch a new company, EnergyOne, to offer the services and obtain revenue from participating distributors and suppliers, in this case AT&T Corp. for telephone service and ADT Ltd. for home security.

Jerry Cosley, a spokesman for Utilicorp, an electric utility based in Kansas City, Mo., said deregulation of the electricity and natural gas markets was giving utilities the chance to market products outside their normal territories.
Two other pairs of utility services also announced plans Tuesday to jointly market services.

Sprint Corp., the No. 3 long-distance company behind AT&T and MCI Communications Corp., set a marketing deal with natural gas provider NorAm Energy Corp. and will test its services with special promotions.
In addition, Suburban Propane Partners LP finalised a marketing agreement with Duke Energy Corp. to offer customers one-stop shopping for propane and natural gas.

"For telephone companies and probably for electrical utilities as well it is no longer a question of profitability any more, but of survival," said Dana Serman, a telecommunications analyst at Schroder Wertheim.

The UtiliCorp/Peco venture will franchise services around the country and hopes to attract customers by offering discounts and the convenience of one-stop shopping. The venture expects to have six utilities and 10 million customers signed up by year-end and is looking for new partners.

"When the U.S. electricity industry is deregulated, the difference in prices between competing services will be very small, so competition will be on the convenience of service," said Dan Rudakas, utilities analyst at Everen Securities.
UtiliCorp had tried selling electricity under the EnergyOne name nationally, but found the effort too expensive.
UtiliCorp Chief Executive Richard Green said utilities have to focus on the service side of the business because that is where the biggest potential profits lie.
"On the gas and electric commodity side of the business, there is a price war relationship with your customer with very slim margins," he told a news conference in Washington.
"Our research indicates that consumers have tired of dealing with multiple suppliers for what are repetitive, essential utility services," said Andrew Guariello, president of EnergyOne.
Analysts said these types of alliances are likely to proliferate.
Schroder's Serman said customers face a bewildering array of services, especially in major cities such as New York.
"We are going to see many more deals along these lines," Serman said.
EnergyOne will act as a clearing house responsible for developing relationships with suppliers, evaluating and selecting new products and services and establishing competitive pricing mechanisms.
Participating utilities will serve as retail distributors of the products, drawing on EnergyOne's identity and support.
Utilicorp stock rose 50 cents to $27.75, ADT rose 87.5 cents to $33.75, AT&T gained 69 cents to $36.94 while Peco edged down 6 cents to $20.44, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
